method_limits: the import test reads the caller file as it is on disk now; a file edited after the row was indexed is graded on its current imports, which is the honest reading of 'where does this call bind today' but not a historical one

only direct name bindings resolve: `from mod import name` and the caller's own `def name` count, while wildcard imports and runtime patching cannot be resolved and are published as their own classes rather than assumed
`from pkg import submodule` is treated as a module import when pkg/submodule.py exists, so a bare call to that word is not credited to a function definition

the write axis is graded on calls inside the definition whose tail is a write verb; a definition that hands its path to a helper is classed by what it does itself, which is the same bound E438 published
the population is E440's shared-name class re-derived from the live corpus; a row whose spelling changed since E440 was published is not in this face

distance_check.reading: the same population E440 published as one class, re-read on the bindings axis

title: resolve each of E440's shared-name bare calls through the caller's own imports and grade whether the surviving definition writes the parameter path itself
